review.summary: Phase 20's offline qualification is genuinely complete, executed, and mechanically bound to the exact reviewed source; publication, tag and terminal CI remain pending delivery obligations by construction. The 59-command gate (docs/reviews/phase-20-attempt-01.checks.json, byte-identical to docs/checks/phase-20.json and to the in-flight chunk attempt-02 snapshot) carries source_sha256 ee60edd5, source_unchanged true, passed true, and all 59 exit codes are 0; I independently re-derived the list from tools/check_phase.py:71-87 (commands_for(17)+commands_for(19) with phase-17-/phase-19- renamed, de-duplicated, plus generate_models --verify-fixtures and both check-native-exports runs) and it reproduces exactly 59, which review_phase.check_evidence:187 enforces by list equality so it cannot be trimmed. Both --require-clean archive proofs bind the current release commit d64d9dc with requireClean true, effectiveDirty false, and identical packaged file inventories (51ea02c8 on 1.89.0, 1e5085b7 on 1.99.0); scripts/check-access-release.py:60-115 ran in-gate and re-reads/re-hashes/re-extracts each retained .local/artifacts crate, compares every packaged byte against both the working tree and git show <releaseCommit>, requires releaseCommit == HEAD, requires the four executed offline examples including the new response_compatibility one, and requires all three external consumer executions. All 14 compiler/feature receipts pass at one common rustInputsSha256 e238f53d, including red-team-json-unification on both compilers, and the 49-job matrix is wired (24 features x 2 toolchains + contracts job) and asserted in tools/test_ci.py and tools/test_release_delivery.py:109-110. A fresh live run exists at crateVersion 0.2.2 whose runtimeInputsSha256 must equal the current runtime fingerprint (tools/live_evidence.py:266), and the gate recorded nativeMethodsVerified 17 / observedMethods 22 with three 403s and two 400s reported honestly and no mutation/cleanup chain claimed. The private-material scan was refreshed at the qualified commit d64d9dc with sourceSha256 equal to the reviewed source, and docs/SECURITY.md:117-123 now documents the --check headCommit semantics, closing chunk finding 3. The new packaged example reproduces precisely the reported G25 failures (opaque job-1/p-1/map-1, space-separated and offset-less timestamps, novel enum vocabulary, unknown nested data), keeps the three disputed structural cases rejected, and asserts Mode::Request still rejects; validation.rs:1198-1229 validates check metadata before skipping only the eight reviewed format kinds plus requestOnly string bounds, with unknown kinds still failing closed; generated.rs:175178-175186 keeps baseline-key collisions hard errors while 175266-175292 suppresses only same-key vendor-added extensions so no duplicate JSON keys are emitted. Documentation is quantitative and honest: CHANGELOG, README, docs/CI.md:168-173, docs/RELEASE.md and docs/PACKAGING.md all state that the 49-job phase-20 workflow has not run and that missing receipts mean publication is unverified. The final gate is rigorous and negatively tested, and a release-readiness record provably cannot advance the phase (review_phase.py:385-386, test_release_delivery.py:165-207). Remaining deficiencies are one medium enforcement/bookkeeping gap whose stated disposition overstates its coverage, plus four low documentation-binding items; no blocker or high finding.

findings.description: The disposition for chunk finding 5 says the current-version publication assertions are "covered_by_final_delivery_guard" and that "the final phase cannot advance without canonical registry/tag receipts matching the qualified archive and remote refs". The second half is true; the first half is not reachable as written. tools/test_ci.py:311-330 selects publications[-1], which is currently the phase-17 0.2.1 record (docs/phase-status.json:3546-3551), so because the workspace version is 0.2.2 the function returns at line 330 and every receipt-specific assertion is skipped, including the CHANGELOG receipt-link check at line 349. tools/release_delivery.py:131-141 reads only delivery.registry_receipt, delivery.tag_receipt and delivery.ci_receipt and never requires a phase-20 registry_publication entry, so a delivery can satisfy the whole guard while publications[-1] still names 0.2.1 and the 0.2.2 receipt links in README.md:40-42, CHANGELOG.md:6-8, docs/RELEASE.md:5-7 and docs/STABILITY.md are never validated against an actual receipt. The receipts themselves are strongly validated by release_delivery.validate_receipts, so this is a documentation-consistency enforcement gap rather than a payload risk.
findings.required_fix: At delivery, add a registry_publication object to the phase-20 record with version "0.2.2" and evidence "docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.2.json" (plus status and source_commit), which makes publications[-1] current and activates the existing tools/test_ci.py receipt-link assertions. docs/phase-status.json is excluded from the source fingerprint (tools/review_phase.py:15-16), so this costs no re-qualification. In a follow-up patch, add an explicit assertion in tools/release_delivery.py:131-141 that phases[20].registry_publication.version == VERSION and that its evidence equals the canonical registry receipt path, and correct this disposition's wording.

findings.description: qualification_attempts[0].resolution still states "clean compiler proofs rerun on corrected candidate 938adbef948e962a5d9b997fbcd078130a175522". That candidate has itself been superseded: both current proofs and the candidate guard bind d64d9dc7f71d95eaa1e7849e661c252660970914 (docs/checks/phase-20-release-package-1.89.0.json:8, docs/checks/phase-20-candidate.json:6), and the 938adbe receipts now live only in the undeclared docs/checks/phase-20-candidate-02/ snapshot. A reader of qualification_attempts is told the wrong release commit, and unlike phase 19 (which declares historical_supplementary_evidence at lines 4145-4171) phase 20 declares no superseded-candidate inventory. The actual commit appears only incidentally in review_findings_disposition finding 3 and candidate_private_scan.head_commit.
findings.required_fix: Update the resolution text to name d64d9dc as the qualified candidate, note that the 938adbe proofs in docs/checks/phase-20-candidate-02/ are preserved but superseded, and add a short superseded-candidate inventory (as phase 19 does) listing phase-20-candidate-01 and phase-20-candidate-02 with their own source hashes. phase-status.json is fingerprint-excluded, so no re-qualification is needed.

findings.description: docs/CI.md:150 states "The complete local Phase 20 gate has 59 commands" and line 158 states "CI's 41-command subset writes phase-20-contracts.json". Both numbers are currently correct (I derived 59 from commands_for(20) and 41 after removing the 14 check-rust, 2 check-native-exports, 1 check-access-release entries and generate_models --verify-fixtures). But unlike the job counts, which tools/test_ci.py asserts via test_current_documented_job_counts_match_the_configured_matrix, no test binds these two numerals: test_ci.py:478-499 only asserts subset relationships and the presence of specific tools, and test_ci.py:44-66 only compares the documented scripts/check-*.py inventory. docs/CI.md:106 similarly hardcodes "41 credential-free commands". Any future change to commands_for(20) would leave three prose counts silently wrong in the document that CI itself is described by.
findings.required_fix: Add an assertion in tools/test_ci.py that the integers parsed from the "complete local Phase 20 gate has N commands" and "N-command subset" / "N credential-free commands" phrases in docs/CI.md equal len(commands_for(20)) and len(ci_commands_for(20)). This changes the source fingerprint, so batch it with the next qualified source change rather than invalidating the current archives.

findings.description: The report discloses that "the time_order effect still parses start_time and end_time timestamp content in response modes and can reject unparseable timestamps or invalid ordering" without saying where it applies. contracts/native-semantics.json:225-236 binds time_order to a single schema (s000196) sourced from src/models/agentguard.ts:142, so the retained refinement touches one AgentGuard root and none of the Red Team reads whose timestamp formats this patch fixes. For a patch whose headline symptom is a timestamp string without RFC 3339 formatting, the generic wording leaves a consumer unable to tell which calls can still fail on a space-separated timestamp, and makes the residual risk read broader than it is.
findings.required_fix: Have tools/g25_report.py emit the owning schema id, source file/line and affected operation(s) for each retained refinement it discloses, so this sentence names the single AgentGuard root instead of describing the effect abstractly. Regenerating the report changes the source fingerprint, so schedule it with the next qualified source change.

findings.description: The typed-over-raw precedence is implemented correctly and without duplicate keys, but for the request-reachable projection models it silently discards caller-supplied data: for TargetMetadata, LanguageOption and the three JobCreateRequestJobMetadataVariant models, a set typed projection causes the same-key extension entry to be skipped during serialization (lines 175266-175292), so a caller who populates both sees their raw value disappear from the request body. This is documented only in markdown (CHANGELOG.md:21-28, docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:17), and the generated projection fields and Extensions carry no rustdoc, so a consumer reading docs.rs for the published 0.2.2 crate cannot discover it. The maintainer has explicitly dispositioned this as markdown-only and does not claim rustdoc was delivered (docs/phase-status.json:4419-4423, 4364-4374), so it is a recorded deferral rather than a misrepresentation.
findings.required_fix: Emit a short generated doc comment on the vendor-added projection fields and on Extensions stating that a set typed projection supersedes a same-key extension on serialization and that callers must leave the projection unset to serialize a preserved raw value. Because this changes the packaged source it must ride a future patch with its own archive proofs, or the markdown-only disposition should be restated as final in the phase-20 record.

tools/release_delivery.py:71-124 cross-checks registry identity, ownership, non-yanked state, per-field equality with proofs[1] (sourceCommit, archiveSha256, archiveBytes, files, vcs), the annotated tag object and its peel, refs/heads/main, terminal run status, the exact per-job context set against the derived matrix, per-job success and unique job URLs, then requires both the published and CI commits to fingerprint to the reviewed source and be ancestors of HEAD. tools/test_release_delivery.py:51-162 exercises missing/extra/duplicate/failed/pending/wrong-run/duplicate-job contexts, stale sources, false summaries, registry and tag tampering, mismatched compiler proofs, and that phase 20 cannot advance when release_delivery.verify raises.

Review governance is current-source bound and readiness cannot complete the phase: tools/review_phase.py:366-367 forbids --release-readiness with chunk/verify/advance, 385-386 refuses advancement unless review_scope is "phase", 390-392 then calls release_delivery.verify, and 239-251 require the phase-20 prompt to begin with the declared scope and embed the exact declared chunk artifacts. tools/test_release_delivery.py:165-207 proves a release-readiness record cannot advance and that relabelling it "phase" invalidates it. I confirmed chunk qualification-and-package is genuinely in attempt 2 at the current source: its attempt-01 record (25 scope paths, source bec9e52c) no longer matches the now 26-path declaration, and the attempt-02 prompt at line 19/36 carries the 26-path scope and the reviewed hash ee60edd5.

Documentation is honest about what has not happened: docs/CI.md:168-173 states that the retained 47-job phase-17 run 21 "is not evidence that the expanded 49-job Phase 20 workflow has run", README.md:40-49 and CHANGELOG.md:5-9 state that the 0.2.2 registry and tag receipts establish publication only when present and that consumers should retain their existing pin until then, and docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:34-38, 50-60 quantify the retained vendor numeric/array constraints, the 213 residual-strictness corpus cases across 6 operations, the uuid 124 / rfc3339 56 / duration 4 format occurrences across 28 operations, and the 172 frozen roots reached by the shared relaxation. No stale archive digest or stale release commit appears in any prose document; the 938adbe digests survive only in the preserved candidate-02 snapshot and the historical chunk review.

The failed first qualification attempt is preserved honestly rather than overwritten: docs/checks/phase-20-candidate-01/phase-20.json:3-6 records passed false at its own source hash 50004755, matching the recorded cause (stale Gateway binding input hash) in docs/phase-status.json:4328-4336. docs/phase-status.json:4442-4446 also records that the chunk reviewer's "56 commands" prose understated the 59-command snapshot, preserving the reviewer output unchanged.
limitations: Read-only review with no shell. I executed nothing: I could not recompute the reviewed source fingerprint ee60edd5, the archive digests 51ea02c8/1e5085b7, the retained .local/artifacts bytes, or any check, and I re-ran no cargo, python, node or tsx command. Every pass claim rests on reading the recorded receipts plus the code that produces and validates them.

Internal consistency is not authentication. docs/PHASES.md:7 states that repository writers and the invoked reviewer tool are trusted and that these hashes detect staleness, not forgery. I cannot confirm the recorded cargo, package or live executions actually occurred, only that their reports are structurally valid, mutually consistent in source hashes and timestamps, and carry plausible compiler banners, durations and outputs.

This is a prepublication readiness record and cannot advance phase 20. Actual registry publication, the immutable v0.2.2 tag and terminal 49-job CI are pending delivery obligations: docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.2.json, docs/checks/release-tag-v0.2.2.json and any docs/checks/phase-20-remote-ci-run-N.json do not exist, so publication, remote source identity and the expanded workflow are unevidenced. I treated these as pending, not as failures.

Both declared chunks are unresolved at this source. qualification-and-package is at attempt 2 with its prompt and checks snapshot written but no record yet, and its accepted attempt-01 record is bound to the earlier source bec9e52c and to a 25-path scope that the now 26-path declaration no longer matches, so it cannot authorize advancement in its current state; registry-and-remote-delivery has no attempts. A fresh complete-phase review after delivery and both accepted chunk reviews is required.

Because release_delivery.verify requires the current fingerprint to equal the reviewed source and both published and CI commits to fingerprint to it, any source change made to address my low findings invalidates the d64d9dc archives and forces re-packaging and re-qualification. I therefore scoped the required fixes accordingly: the medium finding and the two phase-status items are fixable in fingerprint-excluded bookkeeping, while the CI.md, G25 report and rustdoc items should ride a future qualified source change.

scripts/check-package.py is deliberately absent from commands_for(20) because --require-clean demands an empty tree including untracked files, so the archive tests themselves ran outside the recorded gate. Their evidence enters the gate indirectly through check-access-release.py's re-extraction and byte comparison, which I judged sound, but I could not observe the package runs inside the gate record.

Live service acceptance is outside what I can verify. I read docs/checks/phase-08-live-attempt-14.json as a record; the two 400 responses leave the IAM scope-creation and Gateway provisioning mutation and cleanup chains live-unqualified with an SDK request-shape defect explicitly not excluded, and the reported airs-cli-rs loopback suite on worf was not run here.

Per the scoping instruction I did not re-audit historical phase 1-19 infrastructure, the frozen TypeScript baseline, or prior release receipts beyond what this phase's artifacts depend on. I read no credential or tenant-registration file and nothing outside this repository.

I inspected selected generated declarations (the TargetMetadata projection deserialize/serialize paths) rather than the whole 6.7 MB generated model file; generated-model correctness elsewhere rests on the compiler, the executed fixture/oracle checks and the corpus regressions.
